/// Validated, read-only inputs for managed execution.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PreparedExecution {
	pub game_binding: GameBinding,
	pub providers: Vec<ExecutionProvider>,
	pub winners: Vec<ProviderReference>,
	pub visible_files: Vec<ExecutionVisibleFile>,
	pub profile_files: Vec<ExecutionProfileText>,
	pub profile_directory: PathBuf,
	pub data_directory: PathBuf,
	pub cache_directory: PathBuf,
	consumed_state: InstallationState,
	consumed_bytes: Vec<(PathBuf, Vec<u8>)>,
rationale: The summary resembles PreparedExecution, but validated/read-only adds a potentially important invariant. Do not treat as a confident redundancy finding.

name: visible-file-summary
comment: /// One effective Data file, with its backing-file modification time.
rationale: The fields already show path and modified. However, effective and backing-file identify provenance not expressed by SystemTime; ambiguous, not a confident violation.

name: profile-input-summary
comment: /// Resolved Fallout-specific directories and decoded state; no save contents.
rationale: Mostly summarizes fields, but decoded state and exclusion of save contents may define the boundary. Retain unless that contract is documented elsewhere.

name: provider-root-summary
comment: /// A validated provider root supplied by execution composition.
rationale: ProviderRoot already names the entity, but validation provenance may be a caller contract; insufficient evidence for a redundancy finding.

name: execution-error-summary
comment: /// The execution adapter could not configure or launch the upstream view.
rationale: Close to the error name and Display text, but distinguishes configuration and launch failures. Terse public error summaries are not automatically unnecessary.

name: native-failure-summary
comment: /// A bounded failure at the native exception boundary.
rationale: NativeFailure supplies most of the meaning, but bounded exception containment may be an architectural contract. Ambiguous rather than confidently tautological.

name: diagnostic-zero-sentinel
comment: /// A canonical file diagnostic. Line zero identifies a missing key or input.
rationale: The usize line field cannot communicate the zero sentinel meaning; this is a useful API contract.

name: thread-affine-worker
comment:
// The upstream session is thread-affine. Its complete lifetime stays on
						// this blocking worker; only the owned result crosses back to Tokio.
rationale: Explains the external thread-affinity constraint behind keeping the entire session on one blocking worker.

name: utf16-command-line
comment:
// The upstream API takes an already encoded command line, not an argument vector.
// Encode UTF-16 directly so unpaired Windows surrogates are never replaced.
rationale: Explains both the upstream interface constraint and why direct UTF-16 encoding must preserve unpaired surrogates.

name: native-open-safety
rationale: Documents buffer lifetimes, session exclusion, exception containment, and failure ownership instead of merely calling the operation safe.

name: nonrecursive-priority-reason
comment: // Nonrecursive: selecting a low-priority target must not remap its files last.
rationale: Records the domain reason for nonrecursive output-target mapping: output selection must not change priority.

name: fomod-not-semver
comment:
// FOMOD versions are arbitrary-length numeric dot components, not SemVer. Evaluation also needs
// cooperative cancellation and budget accounting, so a SemVer abstraction is unsuitable here.
rationale: Documents a concrete gap in SemVer and the cancellation/budget requirements that justify custom comparison.

name: write-all-control-errors
comment: // Write::write_all retries Interrupted forever, so bridge control signals use distinct non-retryable errors.
rationale: Records a dependency retry contract that explains a surprising error-kind choice.

name: publication-cancellation-boundary
comment:
// mods.toml is the last required canonical mutation. Caller cancellation is no longer
	// observable once that durable rename succeeds.
rationale: Documents the irreversible publication boundary and why cancellation must stop being observed after the durable rename.
